Almost all the above associations are caregiver side.

Maternal attachment anxiety and insecure maternal attachment representations were the predictors in two of the three studies, and only the association with avoidant child attachment concerned the demand side, where it remained preliminary.

The available INS evidence therefore characterises the caregiving system more than the attachment system, and it does so from an attachment perspective, which is worth stating because the two need not behave alike.

Where contingent coordination is itself asymmetric (Beebe et al., 2016), the caregiver's parameters would be expected to bear more heavily upon a symmetric estimate of synchrony, and the remedy is directed estimation.
text.formatted: Where contingent coordination is itself asymmetric <ref type="bibr" target="#b15">(Beebe et al., 2016)</ref>, the caregiver's parameters would be expected to bear more heavily upon a symmetric estimate of synchrony, and the remedy is directed estimation.

text.text: Two of our own studies illustrate this point, since in both the predictor was a caregiving side construct.

Fathers' beliefs about the importance and sensitivity of their own parental role were positively associated with father-child INS during cooperative problem solving (Nguyen, Schleihauf, Kungl, et al., 2021) and, in the structural counterpart of that study, with hypothalamic volume, whereas adult attachment style was not (Long et al., 2021).
text.formatted: Fathers' beliefs about the importance and sensitivity of their own parental role were positively associated with father-child INS during cooperative problem solving <ref type="bibr" target="#b120">(Nguyen, Schleihauf, Kungl, et al., 2021)</ref> and, in the structural counterpart of that study, with hypothalamic volume, whereas adult attachment style was not <ref type="bibr" target="#b91">(Long et al., 2021)</ref>.

text.text: The null attachment result, obtained in the same sample as the caregiving association, is a concrete instance of the separability argued for in Section 2.4, although separable does not mean independent (Section 3.5).
Evidence at the wider level of BBS is clearer with the roles distinguished.
In the empathic stress paradigm, the stressed partner occupies the demand side and the observer the caregiving side for the duration of the measurement.

Inducing psychosocial stress in one member of romantic couples while the other observed, we found higher cortisol resonance in dyads with securely rather than insecurely attached observers, assessed by narrative interview (Gallistl, Handke, et al., 2025).
text.formatted: Inducing psychosocial stress in one member of romantic couples while the other observed, we found higher cortisol resonance in dyads with securely rather than insecurely attached observers, assessed by narrative interview <ref type="bibr" target="#b58">(Gallistl, Handke, et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: In a companion study using self-reported attachment, the presence of an insecure-avoidantly attached partner operated as a stressor rather than a support, with lower psycho-endocrine covariance (Gallistl, Hamann, et al., 2025).
text.formatted: In a companion study using self-reported attachment, the presence of an insecure-avoidantly attached partner operated as a stressor rather than a support, with lower psycho-endocrine covariance <ref type="bibr" target="#b57">(Gallistl, Hamann, et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: Yet, these are again on the observer side and therefore targeting the caregiving system.
Three convergences are worth stating.
The first is demand sensitivity.
Synchrony rises when a dyad is required to perform regulatory or coordinative work.

During cooperation (relative to independent) performance, during handholding under noxious stimulation, and in the presence of an acutely stressed partner (Goldstein et al., 2018; Miller et al., 2019; Nguyen et al., 2020; Gallistl, Handke, et al., 2025).
text.formatted: During cooperation (relative to independent) performance, during handholding under noxious stimulation, and in the presence of an acutely stressed partner <ref type="bibr" target="#b61">(Goldstein et al., 2018;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b111">Miller et al., 2019;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b119">Nguyen et al., 2020;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b58">Gallistl, Handke, et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: This is what a loop recruiting external regulation in proportion to registered prediction error would produce.

Synchrony also rises during conflict and competition (Section 4.2), and coercive exchanges are demanding in exactly the sense at issue, so that a dyad coordinated around the anticipation of aggression satisfies the criterion as fully as one coordinated around its relief.

The discriminating quantity is not the rise but the release, since a loop that terminates upon restoration of the regulated state predicts synchrony that is relinquished once the correction has been delivered, whereas synchrony around an unresolved threat has no termination condition.
The first convergence is in this sense a precondition for the third.
The second convergence is the developmental transfer of regulatory labour described in Section 3.2, which appears to be visible dyadically and not only in isolated participants.
It also is as much a change on the caregiving side as on the attachment side, since it consists in the caregiver relinquishing a mode of regulation that is no longer warranted (Motsan et al., 2021).
text.formatted: It also is as much a change on the caregiving side as on the attachment side, since it consists in the caregiver relinquishing a mode of regulation that is no longer warranted <ref type="bibr" target="#b115">(Motsan et al., 2021)</ref>.

text.text: And the third is that synchrony has been tied most directly to a benefit where a co-regulatory outcome was measured rather than interaction alone (Goldstein et al., 2018; Reindl et al., 2018; Reddan et al., 2020), which is the form our account requires if the currency is metabolic.
text.formatted: And the third is that synchrony has been tied most directly to a benefit where a co-regulatory outcome was measured rather than interaction alone <ref type="bibr" target="#b61">(Goldstein et al., 2018;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b130">Reindl et al., 2018;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b128">Reddan et al., 2020)</ref>, which is the form our account requires if the currency is metabolic.

text.text: The discrepancy concerns the direction of the attachment-related associations.

Greater maternal attachment anxiety accompanied reduced INS during co-viewing (Azhari et al., 2023), whereas insecure maternal representations accompanied elevated INS during cooperative problem solving (Nguyen et al., 2024).
text.formatted: Greater maternal attachment anxiety accompanied reduced INS during co-viewing <ref type="bibr" target="#b9">(Azhari et al., 2023)</ref>, whereas insecure maternal representations accompanied elevated INS during cooperative problem solving <ref type="bibr" target="#b118">(Nguyen et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: A context-specific interpretation is plausible.

Coviewing supplies a shared stimulus without a clear regulatory requirement, so a preoccupied mother may have her predictive resources drawn away from the stimulus whose shared processing the measure indexes.
Instead, cooperative problem solving supplies a live interactive demand, so the same preoccupation may be directed at the partner and raise the measured value.
This interpretation is untested, since it requires the same dyads to be measured under both kinds of demand.
Two further explanations are possible.
The first concerns the construct rather than the context, the two studies having assessed dimensional self-reported anxiety in the one case and interview-assessed representations in the other.
The second concerns timescale.

Attachment has a state as well as a trait expression, and everyday experiences of effective or ineffective support have been reported to shift state attachment in middle childhood against a background of positive carry-over (Verhees et al., 2023).
text.formatted: Attachment has a state as well as a trait expression, and everyday experiences of effective or ineffective support have been reported to shift state attachment in middle childhood against a background of positive carry-over <ref type="bibr" target="#b159">(Verhees et al., 2023)</ref>.

text.text: Conversely, synchrony itself has proved markedly unstable across occasions.

In couples measured twice some weeks apart, heart rat variability synchrony during disagreement showed near-zero correspondence between visits and behaved as a state that any couple might enter rather than as a stable dyadic characteristic (Wilson et al., 2018).
text.formatted: In couples measured twice some weeks apart, heart rat variability synchrony during disagreement showed near-zero correspondence between visits and behaved as a state that any couple might enter rather than as a stable dyadic characteristic <ref type="bibr" target="#b168">(Wilson et al., 2018)</ref>.

text.text: If a trait-level attachment measure is related to a quantity that varies substantially from occasion to occasion, divergence between single-session studies is to be expected on those grounds alone.
The relation between synchrony and interaction quality is similarly conditional.
Our account adds a reason to expect the relation not to hold generally.
Physiological synchrony has been found to be stronger in dyads with more anxious mothers who responded even to small fluctuations in their infant's arousal (Smith et al., 2022).
text.formatted: Physiological synchrony has been found to be stronger in dyads with more anxious mothers who responded even to small fluctuations in their infant's arousal <ref type="bibr" target="#b145">(Smith et al., 2022)</ref>.

text.text: And a systematic review reported greater synchrony with better emotion regulation, and that parenting stress and depression were associated with less synchrony (Sfeir et al., 2026).
text.formatted: And a systematic review reported greater synchrony with better emotion regulation, and that parenting stress and depression were associated with less synchrony <ref type="bibr" target="#b143">(Sfeir et al., 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Both are caregiving side observations, and our account treats them as distinct states rather than as two points on one scale.

Parenting stress and depression deplete the supply side, so investment and hence synchrony should fall, whereas maternal anxiety over-assigns precision to the child's signals, so synchrony should rise.
No single monotonic expectation accommodates both.
The non-monotonicity has also been demonstrated experimentally rather than only observed.

Inducing stress in mothers raised both infant physiological reactivity and mother-infant physiological covariation (Waters et al., 2014), so that a manipulation which worsened the infant's state increased the measure.
text.formatted: Inducing stress in mothers raised both infant physiological reactivity and mother-infant physiological covariation <ref type="bibr" target="#b164">(Waters et al., 2014)</ref>, so that a manipulation which worsened the infant's state increased the measure.

text.text: It shows that covariation can index the transmission of dysregulation rather than its correction.

On our account, the informative quantity is not the central tendency of synchrony but its distribution over time, comprising the degree of departure from alignment, the latency of return, and the variability of both across contexts (Gordon et al., 2025; Müller et al., 2022; Tsubamoto & Horii, 2026).
text.formatted: On our account, the informative quantity is not the central tendency of synchrony but its distribution over time, comprising the degree of departure from alignment, the latency of return, and the variability of both across contexts <ref type="bibr" target="#b62">(Gordon et al., 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b117">Müller et al., 2022;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b156">Tsubamoto & Horii, 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Where the mean is nonetheless the available quantity, we expect its relation to regulatory outcome to have an interior optimum rather than a monotonic form, so that estimators assuming monotonicity are misspecified for it, and a literature testing linear associations would be expected to produce the heterogeneity it has produced.

We therefore predict that curvilinear and moderated specifications, declared in advance rather than fitted following a null linear result, will recover relations on these data that linear models cannot, and that the location of the optimum will shift with demand rather than being fixed.
Two conditions attach to this prediction.
Detecting curvilinearity reliably requires samples appreciably larger than are usual in this literature.

And given the instability of synchrony across occasions noted above, the optimum may be recoverable only within dyads across repeated measurement rather than between dyads measured once, which is a different design from any we have drawn upon and which we specify in Section 6.
This is precisely the question we raised in NAMA without being able to answer it.

Because the methods used to derive INS detect any temporal contingency between two time courses, it remained open whether more synchrony is always better, and we proposed that the degree of desynchronisation and the latency of resynchronisation would prove more informative than the level of synchrony as such (Long et al., 2020; White et al., 2023).
text.formatted: Because the methods used to derive INS detect any temporal contingency between two time courses, it remained open whether more synchrony is always better, and we proposed that the degree of desynchronisation and the latency of resynchronisation would prove more informative than the level of synchrony as such <ref type="bibr" target="#b92">(Long et al., 2020;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b166">White et al., 2023)</ref>.

text.text: Dyadic coordination has since been characterised as a metastable process moving between alignment and segregation (Mayo & Gordon, 2020).
text.formatted: Dyadic coordination has since been characterised as a metastable process moving between alignment and segregation <ref type="bibr" target="#b104">(Mayo & Gordon, 2020)</ref>.

text.text: This was later extended into a theory of flexible multimodal synchrony, in which the informative quantity is flexibility across contexts (Gordon et al., 2025).
text.formatted: This was later extended into a theory of flexible multimodal synchrony, in which the informative quantity is flexibility across contexts <ref type="bibr" target="#b62">(Gordon et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: The developmental evidence is consistent: only a minority of caregiver-child interaction is synchronous, miscoordination and its repair appear beneficial for the child's developing sense of efficacy, and excessive synchrony may indicate intrusive and/or overstimulatory parenting (Markova et al., 2019; Hoehl et al., 2021).
text.formatted: The developmental evidence is consistent: only a minority of caregiver-child interaction is synchronous, miscoordination and its repair appear beneficial for the child's developing sense of efficacy, and excessive synchrony may indicate intrusive and/or overstimulatory parenting <ref type="bibr" target="#b99">(Markova et al., 2019;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b76">Hoehl et al., 2021)</ref>.

text.text: Two further lines of support have since accumulated.
Empirically, the quantity we proposed, has now been measured in an attachment-assessed sample.

In a longitudinal study, a longer latency to interactive reparation during the reunion episode of the Face-to-Face Still-Face procedure at 3 to 8 months predicted insecure attachment at 12 to 24 months (N = 58), and, in a separate analysis of an overlapping subsample (N = 39), children classified as insecure showed higher cortisol reactivity at 5 to 6 years (Müller et al., 2022).
text.formatted: In a longitudinal study, a longer latency to interactive reparation during the reunion episode of the Face-to-Face Still-Face procedure at 3 to 8 months predicted insecure attachment at 12 to 24 months (N = 58), and, in a separate analysis of an overlapping subsample (N = 39), children classified as insecure showed higher cortisol reactivity at 5 to 6 years <ref type="bibr" target="#b117">(Müller et al., 2022)</ref>.

text.text: A direct association between reparation latency and cortisol was not tested.
The two analyses are consistent with a pathway from the dynamics of early interaction, through attachment, to endocrine regulation, but they do not establish it.
What matters for our account, is that the predictive quantity was the latency of return following a mismatch rather than the level of coordination, which is the form our proposal specified.
Constructively, the same asymmetry emerges from a model that was not built to produce it.

In the simulation described in Section 4.1, alignment between parent and infant was not a state the dyad attained and held, but a low-divergence regime punctuated by transient separations and followed by rapid return (Tsubamoto and Horii, 2026).
text.formatted: In the simulation described in Section 4.1, alignment between parent and infant was not a state the dyad attained and held, but a low-divergence regime punctuated by transient separations and followed by rapid return <ref type="bibr" target="#b156">(Tsubamoto and Horii, 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Two points follow.
The informative quantities in that model are time-integrated divergence and the latency of realignment rather than mean similarity, which is the proposal we advanced.
And desynchronisation is not a failure of the dyad but an unavoidable consequence of the partners' asymmetric access to the state being regulated, arising in a system that is functioning as intended.

Our framework therefore predicts an "optimum in the midrange" rather than a monotonic benefit (Beebe & Steele, 2013), since two models that remain aligned irrespective of demand fail to release regulatory load, while two that never align cannot share it.
text.formatted: Our framework therefore predicts an "optimum in the midrange" rather than a monotonic benefit <ref type="bibr" target="#b13">(Beebe & Steele, 2013)</ref>, since two models that remain aligned irrespective of demand fail to release regulatory load, while two that never align cannot share it.

text.text: Adaptive coordination should accordingly include counter-regulation and disengagement alongside matching (Wass et al., 2024).
text.formatted: Adaptive coordination should accordingly include counter-regulation and disengagement alongside matching <ref type="bibr" target="#b161">(Wass et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: The caregiving policy is to correct a deviation, not to reproduce the recipient's state, and there are conditions under which correction requires opposing rather than joining it.
The precedent for an interior optimum is behavioural.

Midrange coordination of vocal rhythms at 4 months was optimal for attachment security at 12 months (Jaffe et al., 2001), and both higher and lower self-and interactive contingency at 4 months predicted insecure and disorganised classifications at 12 months, depending on partner and communication modality (Beebe et al., 2010).
text.formatted: Midrange coordination of vocal rhythms at 4 months was optimal for attachment security at 12 months <ref type="bibr" target="#b80">(Jaffe et al., 2001)</ref>, and both higher and lower self-and interactive contingency at 4 months predicted insecure and disorganised classifications at 12 months, depending on partner and communication modality <ref type="bibr" target="#b14">(Beebe et al., 2010)</ref>.

text.text: The largest test to date supports the form of the prediction but narrows its scope.

In 625 high-risk mother-infant dyads, a model with linear and quadratic terms showed that both very high and very low maternal contingent responsiveness at 4 months predicted disorganised attachment at 18 months, whereas responsiveness was unrelated to security (Mitsven et al., 2022).
text.formatted: In 625 high-risk mother-infant dyads, a model with linear and quadratic terms showed that both very high and very low maternal contingent responsiveness at 4 months predicted disorganised attachment at 18 months, whereas responsiveness was unrelated to security <ref type="bibr" target="#b112">(Mitsven et al., 2022)</ref>.

text.text: In a community sample, rated maternal sensitivity rose with contingent responsiveness only up to a moderate level and fell beyond it (Bornstein & Manian, 2013).
text.formatted: In a community sample, rated maternal sensitivity rose with contingent responsiveness only up to a moderate level and fell beyond it <ref type="bibr" target="#b23">(Bornstein & Manian, 2013)</ref>.

text.text: We are not aware of a physiological or neural study that has tested a quadratic term against an attachment or regulatory outcome.
The two closest studies report moderation rather than curvature.

Greater mother-infant EEG synchrony predicted less infant positive emotion when maternal anxiety was high but was unrelated to it when anxiety was low (Mallin et al., 2026), and higher maternal anxiety predicted lower infant RSA only in dyads with high physiological synchrony (Aitken et al., 2026).
text.formatted: Greater mother-infant EEG synchrony predicted less infant positive emotion when maternal anxiety was high but was unrelated to it when anxiety was low <ref type="bibr" target="#b98">(Mallin et al., 2026)</ref>, and higher maternal anxiety predicted lower infant RSA only in dyads with high physiological synchrony <ref type="bibr" target="#b6">(Aitken et al., 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Three competing models therefore remain open: a monotonic relation, as the cooperative hyperscanning literature implies (Section 4.3); a threshold or plateau, on which synchrony is beneficial up to a level and uninformative beyond it; and a relation whose sign depends on context, whether on the kind of demand, positive under cooperative and negative under conflictual demand (Section 4.2), or on the state of the caregiver, as the two studies just described suggest.

The interior optimum would count as disconfirmed if, in adequately powered designs with repeated measurement within dyads, a quadratic term added nothing to a linear or threshold model of the relation between synchrony and an independently measured regulatory outcome, across more than one kind of demand.
Finally, two things remain unknown.

First, the metabolic quantity in which our account trades, i.e., the cost at which a given regulatory outcome is achieved, has been measured only for the individual and only as a function of a close partner's presence. Masalha et al. (2026) held physiological challenges constant and found the time-integrated deviation from baseline lower in a partner's presence than alone (Section 2.1).
text.formatted: First, the metabolic quantity in which our account trades, i.e., the cost at which a given regulatory outcome is achieved, has been measured only for the individual and only as a function of a close partner's presence. <ref type="bibr" target="#b101">Masalha et al. (2026)</ref> held physiological challenges constant and found the time-integrated deviation from baseline lower in a partner's presence than alone (Section 2.1).

text.text: That work did not assess attachment or caregiving, measured the cost to each participant and not to the dyad, and in the infant experiment compared the mother's presence with a separation, which is itself a demand.
The cost as a function of an attachment and caregiving regime, and the cost to the caregiver and to the dyad, have not been measured.

Inflammatory outcomes have been related to synchrony (Wilson et al., 2018), and endocrine outcomes to attachment classification (Müller et al., 2022), which is nearer to the currency we require than an interaction-quality index, but a marker of accumulated cost is not a measure of the cost of a particular correction.
text.formatted: Inflammatory outcomes have been related to synchrony <ref type="bibr" target="#b168">(Wilson et al., 2018)</ref>, and endocrine outcomes to attachment classification <ref type="bibr" target="#b117">(Müller et al., 2022)</ref>, which is nearer to the currency we require than an interaction-quality index, but a marker of accumulated cost is not a measure of the cost of a particular correction.

text.text: Second, neural flexibility measures have not been applied to attachment-assessed samples, so the claim that flexibility is the more informative quantity in INS remains an expectation.

The remaining gaps, concerning the correlational character of the designs, anatomical coverage and the stability of synchrony across occasions, are set out with the limitations in Section 6 and Table 4.
text.formatted: The remaining gaps, concerning the correlational character of the designs, anatomical coverage and the stability of synchrony across occasions, are set out with the limitations in Section 6 and Table <ref type="table">4</ref>.

text.text: The precision regimes of Section 3.3 can now be projected onto the interacting pair.

We state these as expectations rather than as established findings, and separately for the attachment and caregiving sides, since the same regime may produce different signatures depending on which system it characterises (see Figure 3 and Table 3).
text.formatted: We state these as expectations rather than as established findings, and separately for the attachment and caregiving sides, since the same regime may produce different signatures depending on which system it characterises (see Figure <ref type="figure" target="#fig_4">3</ref> and Table <ref type="table">3</ref>).

text.text: Following Section 4.4, we frame them wherever possible in terms of the temporal profile of synchrony, i.e., its responsiveness to demand, its release, and the latency of return following a departure, rather than its mean level, since the regimes are distinguished by the conditions under which synchrony is entered and relinquished rather than by how much of it obtains on average.
Calibrated precision, which we characterised as secure attachment, should produce synchrony that rises when demand requires it and releases once the correction has been delivered.
Its signature should therefore be flexibility across contexts rather than a uniformly high mean.

On the caregiving side, the corresponding regime grants the partner's signals precision proportional to their informativeness, so that the caregiver detects demand promptly, invests in proportion to it, and withdraws that investment once the correction is made.
Securely attached observers resonated proportionally with a partner's acute stress rather than matching it indiscriminately or ignoring it (Gallistl, Handke, et al., 2025).
text.formatted: Securely attached observers resonated proportionally with a partner's acute stress rather than matching it indiscriminately or ignoring it <ref type="bibr" target="#b58">(Gallistl, Handke, et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: We are not aware of a corresponding attachment side observation.

Because the loop is defined by departure from and return to a regulated state, the regime should be characterised by short latency of return following a rupture, which is the quantity described in Section 4.4.
Deactivation, associated with attachment avoidance, relinquishes the social policy in favour of individual regulation and should produce synchrony that is both lower and less responsive to demand.

This is the direction of the absent cortisol resonance in couples with insecure observers (Gallistl, Handke, et al., 2025) and of the dissociation between subjective and endocrine responding in insecure-avoidant participants (Gallistl, Hamann, et al., 2025).
text.formatted: This is the direction of the absent cortisol resonance in couples with insecure observers <ref type="bibr" target="#b58">(Gallistl, Handke, et al., 2025)</ref> and of the dissociation between subjective and endocrine responding in insecure-avoidant participants <ref type="bibr" target="#b57">(Gallistl, Hamann, et al., 2025</ref>).

text.text: An attachment-side observation points the same way and refines the prediction.

In couples discussing a disagreement, momentary increases in state attachment avoidance were accompanied by heart rate becoming misaligned from the partner's physiology, termed contrarian coregulation, and dispositional avoidance amplified this response (Schreiber et al., 2021).
text.formatted: In couples discussing a disagreement, momentary increases in state attachment avoidance were accompanied by heart rate becoming misaligned from the partner's physiology, termed contrarian coregulation, and dispositional avoidance amplified this response <ref type="bibr" target="#b139">(Schreiber et al., 2021)</ref>.

text.text: The estimate was directed, and the sample was oversampled for personality pathology.
If it generalises, deactivation appears as active misalignment rather than as the mere absence of synchrony, a distinction that only signed or directed estimators can make.
The caregiving side counterpart is a system that does not register the partner's signal as warranting investment.
The two are not distinguishable from synchrony magnitude alone, since a demand that is not made and a demand that is not met both yield a low value.
Directed measures (Section 4.2) and decomposition would separate them.

Where each partner's intrinsic return towards their own baseline is estimated separately from partner-driven synchrony, the two quantities can diverge: in mother-infant interaction, synchronisation from mother to infant was obtained principally among mothers lower in emotion dysregulation, while higher maternal dysregulation was associated with weaker return strength in the infant at reunion (Gao et al., 2023).
text.formatted: Where each partner's intrinsic return towards their own baseline is estimated separately from partner-driven synchrony, the two quantities can diverge: in mother-infant interaction, synchronisation from mother to infant was obtained principally among mothers lower in emotion dysregulation, while higher maternal dysregulation was associated with weaker return strength in the infant at reunion <ref type="bibr" target="#b59">(Gao et al., 2023)</ref>.

text.text: This supplies a supply-side signature that magnitude alone would not distinguish.
Hyperactivation, associated with attachment anxiety, should produce synchrony maintained beyond the point at which co-regulation has been obtained and directed towards signals that do not warrant it.

This accords with the elevated mother-child INS observed with insecure maternal representations during interactive problem solving (Nguyen et al., 2024) and with the elevated autonomic synchrony of more anxious mothers (Smith et al., 2022), both caregiving-side observations.
text.formatted: This accords with the elevated mother-child INS observed with insecure maternal representations during interactive problem solving <ref type="bibr" target="#b118">(Nguyen et al., 2024)</ref> and with the elevated autonomic synchrony of more anxious mothers <ref type="bibr" target="#b145">(Smith et al., 2022)</ref>, both caregiving-side observations.

text.text: On the attachment side, momentary increases in state attachment anxiety were accompanied by heart rate becoming aligned towards the partner's physiology, termed dependent coregulation, most strongly in dispositionally anxious individuals (Schreiber et al., 2021).
text.formatted: On the attachment side, momentary increases in state attachment anxiety were accompanied by heart rate becoming aligned towards the partner's physiology, termed dependent coregulation, most strongly in dispositionally anxious individuals <ref type="bibr" target="#b139">(Schreiber et al., 2021)</ref>.

text.text: If the prior concerning availability is held with low precision under a high volatility estimate, the regime should be marked by instability as much as by level, namely synchrony entered readily, relinquished incompletely, and re-entered on evidence that a calibrated system would absorb without response.

The prediction is therefore of a high mean accompanied by high within-dyad variability and prolonged return following rupture, and it is separable from the caregiving side over-weighting described above, which predicts elevation without the same instability.
Disruption and disorganisation, in which no assignment of precision allows action to discharge error (White et al., 2020), should produce neither sustained synchrony nor its orderly release.
text.formatted: Disruption and disorganisation, in which no assignment of precision allows action to discharge error <ref type="bibr" target="#b167">(White et al., 2020)</ref>, should produce neither sustained synchrony nor its orderly release.

text.text: The only relevant observation we are aware of is at the attentional level and was not statistically robust: infant attachment disorganisation moderated the correspondence between mother and infant monitoring of a separation-reunion animation (Biro et al., 2017).
text.formatted: The only relevant observation we are aware of is at the attentional level and was not statistically robust: infant attachment disorganisation moderated the correspondence between mother and infant monitoring of a separation-reunion animation <ref type="bibr" target="#b20">(Biro et al., 2017)</ref>.

text.text: At the individual level, the defensive hand-blink reflex scaled with the proximity of a threat in adults with organised attachment representations but not in those classified as disorganised, and activating the attachment system moved the two groups in opposite directions (Fossataro et al., 2023).
text.formatted: At the individual level, the defensive hand-blink reflex scaled with the proximity of a threat in adults with organised attachment representations but not in those classified as disorganised, and activating the attachment system moved the two groups in opposite directions <ref type="bibr" target="#b52">(Fossataro et al., 2023)</ref>.

text.text: We read this as graded versus ungraded assignment of precision in proportion to predicted demand.
The finding is individual rather than dyadic, and the sample was small and enriched for disorganised classification.
The account given in Section 3.4 nonetheless yields a more specific expectation than the absence of consolidation.

Where several mutually incompatible predictions concerning the same figure are each held with high precision, the failure is one of arbitration rather than of specification, and its dyadic expression should be synchrony that is entered and abandoned within an episode, with the leading partner reversing, as first one and then another mode governs the exchange, rather than synchrony that is merely weak.

Detecting this requires estimators that recover direction, such as lagged or information-theoretic measures, and, where a signed quantity is available, as in lagged cross-correlation of autonomic series, alternation between positive and negative dependence (Table 3).
text.formatted: Detecting this requires estimators that recover direction, such as lagged or information-theoretic measures, and, where a signed quantity is available, as in lagged cross-correlation of autonomic series, alternation between positive and negative dependence (Table <ref type="table">3</ref>).

text.text: Most INS estimators are non-negative, so sign alternation is not defined for them.
A baseline rate of desynchronisation must be established before any excess can be identified as maladaptive (Section 4.4).

Our account bears most directly on the mismatches identified in Section 2.4, since the metabolic accounting is settled at the junction of the two systems, and these are the cases on which the dyadic literature is close to silent.

Where a fully activated attachment system meets an unresponsive or depleted caregiving system, we expect a dissociation rather than a uniform reduction: sustained or escalating signalling from the demand side against a supply side that is not investing.
This should present as synchrony that fails to consolidate, rather than as synchrony that is simply low, and should be more readily detectable in its direction than in its magnitude.

The divergent parasympathetic pattern under maltreatment severity (Brown et al., 2021) and the dependence of the driving partner on maltreatment subtype (Lunkenheimer et al., 2018), both described in Section 4.2, approximate it.
text.formatted: The divergent parasympathetic pattern under maltreatment severity <ref type="bibr" target="#b26">(Brown et al., 2021)</ref> and the dependence of the driving partner on maltreatment subtype <ref type="bibr" target="#b94">(Lunkenheimer et al., 2018)</ref>, both described in Section 4.2, approximate it.

text.text: Both observations are autonomic and were made in samples not assessed for attachment.

Where the same figure is both the target of the attachment system and the source of the threat activating it, both systems are engaged and neither can complete, and we expect synchrony that neither stabilises nor releases.
Trauma may offer the most informative evidence on flexibility, since the levels of BBS can dissociate within the same dyads.

In a cohort of war-exposed children and their mothers, dyads meeting criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder showed the tightest autonomic and the lowest behavioural synchrony, whereas resilient dyads showed the highest behavioural and the lowest autonomic synchrony.

text.text: The dyadic evidence therefore neither confirms the individual account developed in Section 3 nor counts against it.
It leaves a substantial area unexamined, comprising the mismatch between the two systems at the neural level, the metabolic quantity itself, and the group level.
Because synchrony has proved unstable across occasions (Section 4.4), none of these expectations can be tested adequately at a single measurement.
Section 6 sets out what the requisite designs would need to do.
>Clinical and practical implications
text.formatted: <head n="5." >Clinical and practical implications</head>

text.text: Our account has consequences for how attachment is assessed and for how attachment-related change is understood.
We state five.

Following Sections 2.4 and 4.1, we state them separately for the attachment and the caregiving system wherever the two diverge, since the same dyadic observation carries different implications depending on which system it characterises.

If synchrony indexes, as we hypothesise, where predictive and regulatory work is being invested, rather than the state a dyad is coordinating around (Section 4.2), a clinically important consequence follows immediately: a dyad may be tightly coordinated around the anticipation of aggression, and coordination of that kind is an accrual of load rather than its distribution.

An intervention that increases proximity, contingency or synchrony is therefore not therapeutic in itself, and where the relationship is a source of threat it may entrench the coordination it is intended to improve.

Felt security is a constructed inference that ordinarily tracks the actual state of the world, and it cannot be reinstated while a genuine threat from within the relationship persists, because the model correctly predicts a shortfall between demand and available resources.
Where adversity is current rather than historical, the first requirement is a change in the conditions themselves, and an intervention directed at the felt state alone is misdirected.

Assessment should, accordingly, establish whether a relationship is safe enough to serve as a regulatory resource before it asks how well the pair co-regulate, and dyadic work is contraindicated where it would increase danger or extend a coercive partner's control.

text.text: Two recommendations follow.

A dyadic index should not be reported as a single measure of the relationship, but accompanied by separate characterisation of both partners' systems, with the roles held fixed for the duration of the measurement wherever the design permits.
Change.

Because the precision regimes and the internal working models (IWMs) that weight them are learned, they remain open to revision whenever incoming evidence is granted sufficient precision to update them (Section 3.3).
Earned security (Roisman et al., 2002) and therapeutic improvement (Taylor et al., 2015) are, on this reading, instances of model updating rather than of a fixed disposition overcome.

text.text: We take these as the strongest available evidence bearing on the mechanism our account proposes, since what is manipulated is caregiver behaviour and what changes is an allostatic parameter in the other body.
The mechanism itself, including our reading of the change in sensitivity as a change in caregiving-side precision, remains open.
Four qualifications attach to this.
The first is that revision does not require erasure.

On the reading set out in Section 2.4, a multistable system holds a newer and context-appropriate model as an attractor alongside the older insecure one, rather than replacing it, and under stress, the basin of the older and more precisely held model deepens and activity is captured by it.
The re-emergence of an earlier pattern under load is therefore what our account predicts, and not evidence that change did not occur.
Treatment can be asked to secure the preservation of flexibility under demand rather than the removal of the older model (Bosmans et al., 2020 (Bosmans et al., , 2022)).

text.text: The second is that the supply side is itself a variable.
The therapist, and the caregiver in a parenting intervention, occupies the caregiving side, and the caregiving system has its own precision regime and its own budget.

Parenting stress and depression have been associated with reduced synchrony and maternal anxiety with elevated synchrony (Smith et al., 2022; Sfeir et al., 2026), and our account treats these as opposite states rather than as two points on one scale (Section 4.4).

text.text: They accordingly call for opposite first moves, replenishment of a depleted supply side in the one case and recalibration of an over-assigned precision in the other.

The third is that a prior held with a precision that resists correction may discount evidence of availability rather than incorporate it, so that the rate at which a relationship can be granted evidential weight is part of what treatment must address.

Early adversity has been reported to impair the capacity to use familiar others as buffers later in development (Gunnar, 2017; Hostinar & Gunnar, 2013), so that the regulatory resource a treatment offers may not initially be usable by the person to whom it is offered, and its usability is itself among the things treatment must build.

text.text: The fourth is that the target is calibration and not maximisation.

The calibrated regime of Section 3.3 grants a partner's signals precision proportional to their informativeness and relinquishes investment once the correction has been delivered, and the optimum we expect lies in the midrange rather than at the maximum (Section 4.4).

What treatment should aim at is flexible movement between regulation performed with another and regulation performed alone, these being on the reading of Section 3.2 the same computation differing in where it is carried out.
The two disruption routes.
If the distinction drawn in Section 3.4 holds, it identifies distinct treatment targets rather than degrees of a single severity.
Where the caregiver is present but is itself the source of threat, the maltreatment route installs a standing, high-precision prediction of threat that no policy discharges.

Its clinical problem is a danger prior insulated from correction, and the corresponding requirement is the re-establishment of conditions under which disconfirming evidence can revise the model rather than be assimilated to it (White et al., 2020; Kotler et al., 2026).
text.formatted: Its clinical problem is a danger prior insulated from correction, and the corresponding requirement is the re-establishment of conditions under which disconfirming evidence can revise the model rather than be assimilated to it <ref type="bibr" target="#b167">(White et al., 2020;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b85">Kotler et al., 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Where the caregiver is absent, the neglect route installs a a confidently held expectation that no action will resolve the deviation, together with a collapse of policy precision.
Its clinical problem is disengagement rather than defence, and the corresponding requirement is the restoration of an expectation of efficacy (Section 3.4).

Because disorganised attachment is neither a sensitive nor a specific marker of maltreatment (Granqvist et al., 2017), neither route can be inferred from a presentation, and the caregiving history is required for either judgement.
text.formatted: Because disorganised attachment is neither a sensitive nor a specific marker of maltreatment <ref type="bibr" target="#b64">(Granqvist et al., 2017)</ref>, neither route can be inferred from a presentation, and the caregiving history is required for either judgement.

text.text: A caution is attached to both routes.
Where the attachment system has been organised around a figure that was itself threatening, proximity may reactivate the prediction rather than revise it.
Predictable boundaries, titrated contact and the person's own control over proximity are therefore conditions under which the evidence a relationship offers can be granted precision at all.
Our framework we have set out is a theoretical proposal, and social allostasis is not a diagnostic category.

The synchrony measures discussed above are research instruments whose relation to the latent quantities our account posits has not been established (Section 4.4), their values depend upon task, timing, age, analytic method and modality, and no threshold exists by which an individual dyad may be classified.

The experimental evidence is confined to a small number of caregiving intervention trials, and normalisation of a physiological index is not itself evidence of improved safety, functioning or relational quality.

We accordingly offer the foregoing as a framework for formulation and as a specification of what would be worth measuring, rather than as a basis for present clinical decision-making about individuals.
Three persistent misconceptions.
Three claims remain prominent in attachment-and trauma-informed practice that our framework does not support, although each rests on a clinical observation worth retaining.
The first is that attachment and therapeutic change are organised in the right hemisphere (Schore, 2022).

text.text: The body is central to the traumatic process, but the storage metaphor mislocates the mechanism.

On a predictive account, what endures is a set of danger priors held with a precision that resists correction, expressed in the body through altered autonomic and endocrine regulation (Section 3.4), plausibly stabilised in part by epigenetic regulation of stress-responsive genes such as the glucocorticoid receptor (Turecki & Meaney, 2016; Weaver et al., 2004), and open to revision (Kotler et al., 2026).

text.text: The clinical intuitions behind all three claims are retained by the account we have set out.

The core of our account, namely the reading of the four NAMA modules as components of one predictive allostatic loop and of the organised styles as precision regimes over that loop, is a specification at the level of computational function, stated in Box 2 so that it can be implemented.

It retains our earlier work's anatomical and neurochemical claims intact and adds a unifying principle from which their arrangement can be derived (Long et al., 2020; White et al., 2020; Izaki et al., 2024).
text.formatted: It retains our earlier work's anatomical and neurochemical claims intact and adds a unifying principle from which their arrangement can be derived <ref type="bibr" target="#b92">(Long et al., 2020;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b167">White et al., 2020;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b79">Izaki et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: Its value is accordingly that of an extended framework that generates predictions rather than that of an established mechanism.
The evidential status is not uniform across the account.

The single mapping is consistent with the anatomy of the allostatic interoceptive system and with the simulation of the organised styles as parameter settings of a common loop (Cittern et al., 2018; J. Zhang et al., 2025).

text.text: The projection of the precision regimes onto the dyad, and the mapping of particular regimes onto particular synchrony signatures, are stated as expectations to be tested and not as findings the literature currently supports (Sections 4.4 and 4.5).

The attachment-specific evidence is preliminary, the direction of the reported associations is not fixed, and no design has yet separated the three explanations of the divergence offered in Section 4.4.
Ten limitations are illustrated in Table 4.

text.text: Summarised very briefly here, these limitations concern (1) the measurement of attachment separately from interpersonal closeness (Section 4.3); (2) the separation of the attachment and caregiving systems, which most designs do not achieve, so that the available attachment-related synchrony evidence is predominantly caregiving side (Section 4.3); (3) the symmetry of the estimators in general use (Section 4.2); (4) the absence, in much of the literature, of controls for common input and task structure (Section 4.2); (5) the metabolic quantity, which has been measured only for the individual and not as a function of attachment or caregiving regime (Sections 2.1 and 4.4); (6) the concentration of hyperscanning on dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and the temporo-parietal junction (Section 4.4); (7) the status of metastability as a proposed rather than an established marker (Kotler et al., 2026); (8) the correlational character of most designs (Moreau & Dumas, 2021; Novembre & Iannetti, 2021); (9) the instability of synchrony across occasions, which almost every study has measured once (Wilson et al., 2018); and (10) the modelling of the relation between synchrony and regulatory outcome as monotonic (Section 4.4).

text.text: The second follows from the instability noted above and is a precondition for most of what follows.
Designs should sample repeatedly within dyads, across occasions and across levels and kinds of demand, rather than estimating synchrony once.
Models should also be specified to allow non-monotonic relations, declared in advance rather than fitted after a null linear result, and should separate within-dyad from between-dyad variation.

And because the reliable detection of curvilinearity requires samples appreciably larger than are usual in this literature, the design that is most likely to succeed is intensive repeated measurement of fewer dyads rather than single assessment of more (Moffat & Cross, 2026).
text.formatted: And because the reliable detection of curvilinearity requires samples appreciably larger than are usual in this literature, the design that is most likely to succeed is intensive repeated measurement of fewer dyads rather than single assessment of more <ref type="bibr" target="#b113">(Moffat & Cross, 2026)</ref>.

text.text: The third is to pair hyperscanning and BBS assessment with validated interview, observational or questionnaire measures of attachment rather than with proxies for closeness, so that the attachment dimension and the closeness gradient can be estimated independently, as the more recent studies have begun to do.
The fourth follows from the two-system extension and is, in our view, the most consequential.

Designs should fix the two attachment and caregiving roles for the duration of a measurement, assess the attachment and caregiving system of both partners rather than one of them, and apply directed estimators so that the asymmetry of investment becomes an observable rather than an assumption.

Every design should include surrogate or pseudo-dyad controls and should record gaze, speech and/or movement, so that dependence arising from common input and shared task structure can be estimated and separated from dependence arising from the interaction itself (Section 4.2).
Designs should also assess the caregiving system with caregiving strategy measures rather than through the caregiver's attachment orientation (Colledani et al., 2022).
text.formatted: Designs should also assess the caregiving system with caregiving strategy measures rather than through the caregiver's attachment orientation <ref type="bibr" target="#b38">(Colledani et al., 2022)</ref>.

text.text: For high-risk or clinical dyads, a further requirement is interpretive as well as ethical.

Because synchrony may reflect coordination around threat as readily as coordination towards its relief (Section 4.2), safety, coercion and power asymmetry within the relationship must be assessed directly rather than inferred from the synchrony itself, and a measured value obtained without them is not interpretable in the terms our account proposes.

The fifth is to impose graded regulatory demand, through stress induction, acute pain, or cooperative problem solving, and to manipulate the availability of co-regulation directly, so that synchrony can be tied to a regulatory outcome and the prediction that co-regulation lowers the cost of achieving it can be placed at risk.

Demand should be varied in kind as well as in degree, since synchrony rises under conflictual and competitive demand as it does under cooperative demand (Section 4.2), and a design that varies intensity alone cannot distinguish the two.
The sixth is to index the metabolic quantity itself.

We define it operationally as the timeintegrated deviation of an autonomic, endocrine or metabolic signal from its baseline until a criterion return, i.e., the incremental area under the curve, under a challenge held constant across conditions.

This quantity is measurable and independent of any synchrony estimate, and it has been used to show that a close partner's presence lowers the cost of standard homeostatic challenges (Masalha et al., 2026).
text.formatted: This quantity is measurable and independent of any synchrony estimate, and it has been used to show that a close partner's presence lowers the cost of standard homeostatic challenges <ref type="bibr" target="#b101">(Masalha et al., 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Our account adds requirements to the design around it.
Both partners should be measured with their roles fixed, so that the recipient's cost, the caregiver's cost and their sum can be computed separately.
Attachment and caregiving regimes should be assessed in both partners.
And the comparison condition should remove the partner's regulatory contribution without imposing a separation, since separation in infancy is itself a demand.
Because the modalities are not interchangeable (Reindl et al., 2022), they should be modelled jointly rather than treated as substitutable indices of one dyadic state.
text.formatted: Because the modalities are not interchangeable <ref type="bibr" target="#b131">(Reindl et al., 2022)</ref>, they should be modelled jointly rather than treated as substitutable indices of one dyadic state.

text.text: The seventh is to adopt longitudinal designs, in which earned security and therapeutic change are operationalised as measurable shifts in prior precision, in which the persistence of an older model alongside a newer one is tested by re-assessment under load rather than at rest, and in which the two disruption routes are followed as dissociable trajectories rather than inferred from a single presentation.

Randomised caregiving interventions already manipulate the caregiving side and measure allostatic outcomes (Bernard, Dozier, et al., 2015; Bernard, Hostinar, et al., 2015; Cicchetti et al., 2011; Garnett et al., 2020; Section 5.1), and the addition to them that our framework calls for is the measurement of mechanism alongside outcome, so that a change in the recipient's allostatic parameters can be referred to an estimated change in the caregiver's precision regime rather than to the intervention as a whole.

We have moved the account from one brain to two, and the dyad is where measurement is presently feasible.

Moving to the dyad required two extensions.

We propose that the partner in an interacting pair is ordinarily not running a second copy of the attachment loop, but the complementary and asymmetric caregiving system, which is activated by another's signalled or anticipated distress and terminates in the alleviation of that distress.
Therefore, what is distributed across a dyad is regulatory work, although the two partners do not perform the same work, and the metabolic accounting is settled at the junction of the two systems.

Our proposal belongs to the line of work that moved second-person neuroscience towards computational models of reciprocal interaction (Bolis et al., 2017; Lehmann et al., 2024), and joins a small but rapidly growing set of accounts that treat the caregiving dyad in predictive and regulatory terms (Cittern et al., 2018; Diaz-Rojas et al., 2025; Santaguida et al., 2026; Tottenham and Vannucci, 2025; Tsubamoto and Horii, 2026).

text.text: The rationale for adopting our framework is integrative.

It does not displace the anatomy, the neurochemistry, or the dyadic measurement of our earlier work, but supplies a single regulatory principle from which their arrangement follows, and against which organised, disrupted, and disorganised attachment can be expressed as settings of a common loop rather than as separate descriptions.
We would like to close with two remarks.
The first names the claim on which our account is most exposed.

Its organising proposition is that the currency in which attachment trades is metabolic, so that the calibrated dyad is distinguished from the miscalibrated one by the cost at which a given regulatory outcome is obtained, rather than by the amount of coordination it displays.

text.text: We therefore adopt a strict criterion.

A co-regulatory reading of synchrony requires that synchrony predicts, or statistically mediates, a regulatory change measured independently of the synchrony estimate, and it is strengthened where directed estimators show that the change in the recipient follows the partner's input rather than preceding it.
Without such a signature, synchrony licenses no co-regulatory inference.

text.text: This is the best-supported generalisation in the area.
One boundary condition should nonetheless be attached to it.

The paradigms from which the generalisation is drawn, are overwhelmingly cooperative or neutral in valence, and the developmental hyperscanning literature rarely induces conflict, competition or coercion.

The monotonic relation between synchrony and interaction quality is therefore established across a restricted range of interaction types, and the findings reviewed in Section 4.2, in which synchrony rose during conflict and competition and predicted costly outcomes, fall outside that range.
We take the generalisation to hold within the conditions under which it has been tested rather than as a property of synchrony as such.
At the level of attachment, the evidence is preliminary and does not establish that INS varies systematically with individual differences.

A successful intervention may first raise coordination, as partners become more engaged with one another, and only later lower it, as regulation becomes more differentiated; and a fall may equally reflect healthy differentiation or withdrawal.

The quantities our account would put in its place are the latency from perturbation to repair, the frequency of transitions into high-arousal or disengaged states, and flexibility across contexts, of which the first has already been measured in an attachment-assessed sample (Section 4.4).

Such quantities require repeated measurement, since synchrony has proved unstable across occasions (Section 4.4).
And they require concurrent behavioural and subjective data, since no synchrony measure discloses on its own which of two opposite changes has occurred.

text.text: What our account would contribute to such work is the architecture, namely four modules as components of one loop with two balances between them, together with the disrupted and disorganised configurations that none of these models at present represents.

Such an implementation can place the central proposition at risk only if the simulated agent carries an explicit energetic state and a cost for each action, since an agent that minimises free energy will otherwise show lower cumulative free energy for calibrated regimes by construction.

With those terms in place, a simulation could test whether calibrated regimes restore the regulated state at a lower energetic cost than miscalibrated ones, whether a multimodal prior yields contradiction where two modes compete and disorientation where more than two do, and whether an activated demand side meeting a depleted supply side yields synchrony that fails to consolidate.
A working implementation shows that an architecture is sufficient to produce a pattern, not that the biological system produces it in that way.
